hook_type.instructions: Which kind of opening does the post use in its first sentence, first slide or first two seconds?

criteria.number_or_list: Opens on a number or a count of items ("3 fixes", "7 tools").
criteria.question: Opens by asking the viewer a question.
criteria.bold_claim: Opens on a strong or surprising statement.
criteria.contrarian: Opens by saying a common belief or habit is wrong.
criteria.problem: Opens on a pain or a mistake the viewer has.
criteria.result_first: Opens by showing or stating the end result.
criteria.story: Opens on a personal moment or anecdote.
criteria.how_to: Opens by promising to teach a specific thing.
criteria.other: None of the above, or no clear opening.

first_frame.instructions: What does the first frame or first slide mainly show?

criteria.face: A person's face, talking or reacting.
criteria.text_only: Words on a plain or blurred background.
criteria.screen_or_product: A screen recording, an app or a product.
criteria.action: Something happening: a place, a process, hands at work.
criteria.graphic: A chart, a diagram, an illustration or a meme image.
criteria.unknown: The picture is not available, so it cannot be told.

criteria.talking_head: One person speaking to the camera for most of it.
criteria.voiceover: A voice over footage, stills or animation, with no speaker on camera.
criteria.screen_recording: Mostly a recorded screen or app walkthrough.
criteria.carousel: A set of still slides the viewer swipes through.
criteria.demo: A product or process shown working.
criteria.montage: Clips cut to music with little or no speech.

angle.instructions: What is the post's main angle on its topic?

criteria.teach: Explains how to do something, step by step or as tips.
criteria.mistake: Warns about an error and what to do instead.
criteria.personal_story: Tells what happened to the creator or a customer.
criteria.comparison: Sets two or more options against each other.
criteria.proof: Shows a result, a number or a case as evidence.

pacing.instructions: How fast does the post move from one idea or shot to the next?
criteria: Slow: one idea or shot held for a long time.
Steady: a new idea or shot every several seconds.
Fast: a new idea or shot every two or three seconds.
Very fast: cuts or new lines about every second.

call_to_action.instructions: What does the post ask the viewer to do, in its words, its last frame or its caption?

criteria.comment: Comment, reply or answer a question.
criteria.save_or_share: Save the post or send it to someone.
criteria.link_or_buy: Visit a link, sign up, download or buy.

face_on_camera.instructions: Is a person's face visible on camera for a meaningful part of the post?

criteria.true: A face is on screen for much of it.
criteria.false: No face, or only a brief glimpse.

text_on_screen.instructions: How much written text is shown on screen?
criteria: A title or a few words.
Captions or text for most of the post.
Text is the main content, as in a text slide.

criteria.stills: A carousel or a single image.
criteria.unknown: The media is not available, so it cannot be told.

names_audience.instructions: Does the post say who it is for, by naming a kind of person, role or situation?

criteria.true: A viewer can tell who is being addressed ("founders", "if you run payroll").
criteria.false: It could be addressed to anyone.

concrete_detail.instructions: Does the opening contain a specific number, name, time span or result?

criteria.true: It states a figure, a named thing or a measurable outcome.

production.instructions: How produced does the post look?
criteria: Raw: one take on a phone, no edits.
Designed: graphics, b-roll, sound design or motion.
